_comment: Indicators this repository observed directly on a live account, rather than values a published source stated. It exists because the other dossier-shaped files cannot hold these: x-dossiers.json records what a researcher's post says, and third-party-registries.json what a registry publishes, while a value read off an account by a maintainer is neither. Records here carry the `curated` provenance label, which is what that label means. Every entry cites the page the value was read from and the date it was read, because an account can change or vanish and the observation is only ever true as of that day. Values are normalized on load by the same normalizer the scraper uses, so an address recorded here and the same address later matched in a report collapse to one record. Persona names must match the spelling used in x-dossiers.json, or the entry will anchor a second persona page instead of joining the existing one. A photograph from a pipu.cc listing is filed with face: false and a reused_on count: a perceptual hash over every thumbnail in the set (21 September 2026) showed 519 product images each attached to two or more listings under different names, so a listing's image is drawn from a pool and says nothing about the person on the CV. See docs/pipu-lead-screening.md.

dossiers.note: Read from the account's own LinkedIn activity on 31 August 2026, where it appears twice in comments the account left on other people's posts, each asking to be contacted at that address. It is the account publishing its own contact address in public, not a value any researcher reported. The same profile states ten years of web development experience while LinkedIn's own account history gives its join date as May 2025, and on 31 August 2026 it listed no employment or education entries at all. Re-read on 12 September 2026, the same profile now carries five roles running back to March 2014 -- ThriveCart, the Mautic community, Creuna, Intechnica and Avenis Oy -- a degree from James Cook University in Singapore dated 2009 to 2013, two projects, and an open-to-work banner. An employment history reaching eleven years back, filled in on an account LinkedIn dates to May 2025 and after the account was first recorded as having none, is the observation here; whether the roles are real is not something this site establishes.

dossiers.note: Read on 21 September 2026 from a listing on the pipu.cc marketplace whose product description is this curriculum vitae, one of 1,882 such listings posted between 26 June and 2 July 2025 from seller accounts named after each CV's subject. The listing carries a photograph as its product image; it is the same photograph four other listings in the set carry under four other names, so it is not shown here and is not evidence of anyone's face. What ties this listing to the index is the GitHub account printed on the CV, princecharming0115, read directly on 21 September 2026. The account was created in October 2022 and holds 25 repositories. Its own commits are signed coolprince0115@gmail.com 491 times and, once, on the repository it created most recently, dsalo0915@gmail.com, the address the CV gives. Two of its repositories, exoid-did-wallet-backend and did-wallet-verifier-widget, hold 44 commits by a second account, arturdranhoi, signed artur.dranhoi@exiod.io and artur.dranhoi@exoid.io, beside commits by a developer at Exoid, the company whose product they are; the CV describes that product, a decentralised-identity wallet with zero-knowledge proofs built for a DIFC Court notarisation project, as this persona's own work. unattributed.label: Former GitHub handles recovered from the account id in commit noreply addresses
unattributed.note:
A GitHub noreply address is minted from the account's immutable numeric id, in the form id+handle@users.noreply.github.com, and the handle in it is whatever the account was called when the commit was made. Walking the commit history of the accounts this index already holds therefore recovers their previous names as a matter of record rather than as an inference: the same numeric id under two handles is one account, and GitHub's own API resolves an id to whatever that account is called today.

Thirty-two of the walked accounts turned out to have been renamed at least once, yielding 51 former handles. Every one of the thirty-two numeric ids resolves to an account this index already holds, so nothing here names a new account; what it adds is the earlier names, which is what a search of older reporting would turn up. The mapping, current name first: accompany1205 was prince2115, graeme2115; admin-0123 was nicolas-95, achiever0123; AMagicHarry was besthonestman; apollo0102 was peterjiro; attractiveDev was phoenix10221004; bitcrusher1023 was shinystar-0314; blockbusterdev was devtwinkler, softvoyager, talenteddev36428; CleverSofter was miss0702; codomposer was gitakileus; coinyx was cryptobunny0x, techtrust0x0, trust023, techtruth1; cryptostar7 was lucaslee129, harbon486; DreamHigh0806 was ssguardheaker; dtorres314 was trustme000777, whimsyrover; eros1006 was dedicatedsoftwaredev, fredericrowe; erosyj was xfika, greengarden510; euri21 was solution888; h918m was topdev707; icetrust0212 was trust0212, sergey0142; jusdy was dylandev125, pauleta0126; kstar0102 was wangjin0102; prodev90 was prodev1991715; resplegend was trust0212-fantohm; smartgeek1003 was olderdev523, olderdev1003; SoftwarePassioner was care823; starmastar1126 was ministar1126; Stenor5 was luckydev0515, stenor0515; Talented0Dev was createnewhistory; Talentedtopcoder was topcoderben, benjaminstewart123; top-dev-999 was vitaliy-egorov; wenMoonx was yucob; whisdev was ptcbink, ptc-bink, sakele1026.

Seven of these former handles are already published in this index as separate github_profile indicators, recorded before the rename was known: trust0212, trust0212-fantohm, dylandev125, xfika, greengarden510, gitakileus and olderdev523. All seven now return 404, and all seven are the same accounts as icetrust0212, resplegend, jusdy, erosyj, erosyj, codomposer and smartgeek1003 respectively, which this index also holds. They are kept rather than removed, because a dead handle is still the right thing to find in a report written while it was live, but a reader should not count them as separate accounts.

These are recorded as usernames rather than as profile URLs on purpose. 49 of the 51 are unregistered today, and an unregistered handle can be taken by anyone, at which point a published URL would point at a stranger. That is not hypothetical here: yamamotojiro, formerly DreamHigh0806, and fancydeveloper, formerly BitFancy, have both been re-registered by unrelated accounts under different numeric ids. Neither is published as a value in this entry for that reason, and neither should be treated as an indicator of anything.

Read on 20 September 2026 by resolving every numeric id found in the noreply addresses captured by the commit walk of 19 September. No persona is attached: these are earlier names for accounts already filed, and recovering a name supplies no attribution the index did not already have.

unattributed.label: A second account of the holder behind starmastar1126, committing under the same display name
unattributed.note:
github.com/starmaster1126 is GitHub account id 52027648, created on 20 June 2019, and is a different account from github.com/starmastar1126, which is id 67782634 and which this index already holds under "Accounts tied to the mr.new0509 address by email reuse". The two handles differ by one letter, starmastER against starmastAR, and both end in 1126.

The link is the display name rather than the handle. Walking the repositories of starmastar1126 on 19 September 2026 recovers 50 commits authored by 52027648+starmaster1126@users.noreply.github.com under the name Silas Jo. The same repositories carry two commits from 67782634+ministar1126@users.noreply.github.com, also under the name Silas Jo, and that address belongs to the held account itself: GitHub mints a noreply address from the account's immutable numeric id, and 67782634 is starmastar1126 under a former handle. The candidate therefore commits under a name the held account uses of itself, which is the test this index applies to separate a holder's own second identity from the upstream author of a repository that was copied in.

Two further details agree with that reading without being relied on for it. The profile name on starmaster1126 is StarMaster DevGenius, against the StarMastar DevGenius that the held account signs its own commits with, again one letter apart. And both of the candidate's public repositories were created and last pushed on 21 October 2019, the same-day pattern that separates these accounts from ordinary ones.

What is not filed here is worth recording too. github.com/dylanwilliams1126, account id 170390436, also commits into starmastar1126 and its address dylanwilliams1126@gmail.com appears in that account's history, but it does so once and under its own name rather than one the held account uses. One commit under an unshared name is what an ordinary contributor looks like, so it is left out. The same applies to the other accounts a ranking pass surfaced on 20 September 2026: committing into a held account's repository is how that pass selected them in the first place and is not evidence of anything on its own.

The account was live when read on 20 September 2026. No persona is attached, because the group it joins carries none.

unattributed.label: Names the "Saja network portfolio accounts (Nisos)" accounts present under, tied to specific accounts
unattributed.note:
The entry for this group in x-dossiers.json records that Nisos named Jan Kowalski on one portfolio's about section, and Kornel Dudek, Fred Rowe, Juan Pablo Torres and Thomas Richard in the sites' testimonials, but that none of those names was tied to a particular account and so none was recorded. Reading the accounts themselves supplies what was missing for some of them.

Three of the names are what the accounts put in their own GitHub profile name field, read from the API on 20 September 2026: CleverSofter gives Marcin Pawlak, SoftwarePassioner gives Damian Kowalczyk, and Ideal-Softer gives Taylor Fuller. These are not inferred from anything; they are the value the account publishes about itself.

Three more come from the commit walk of 19 September 2026, and are more interesting because they cross accounts. Jiners Enoheart signs commits from three distinct GitHub account ids — 160272094, 160324684 and 36896525, which are CleverSofter, SoftwarePassioner and Ideal-Softer. Leon Hoffmann signs commits from two, 38037508 and 38038194, which are eros1006 and VeteranSoftDev. Jan Kowalski, the one name the report did publish, signs commits from four: eros1006, websparkledev, VeteranSoftDev and nulidev. A GitHub noreply address is minted from the account's immutable numeric id, so "the same name from several ids" is a statement about accounts rather than about spellings.

Jan Kowalski should not be searched as though it identified anybody. It is the standard Polish placeholder name, the equivalent of John Doe in English, and it is recorded here only because it now attaches to four specific accounts rather than floating in a report. Marcin Pawlak and Damian Kowalczyk are likewise ordinary Polish names and Taylor Fuller an ordinary English one; Jiners Enoheart is the only one of the six distinctive enough that a match on it means much. Their value is that they agree with what Nisos assessed, a network posing as Polish and United States developers, and that they give a reader something to check a job application against.

A name here settles nothing about any person. These are the identities the accounts wear, and the people whose names they may have been assembled from are as likely to be uninvolved as not. Nothing on this entry is an assertion that a person of any of these names exists, is a DPRK operator, or has done anything at all.

unattributed.label: GitHub accounts working in the same repositories as the Eric Liu persona
unattributed.note:
Read on 24 September 2026. lazarus.group attributes three GitHub accounts to the Eric Liu persona, github.com/vigorousdeveloper, github.com/SuperVenus0725 and github.com/Jason07250000, with the commit addresses vigorousdevelopment524@gmail.com and venus07250000@gmail.com; tayvano lists the same accounts. Searching GitHub for commits signed with those two addresses finds them inside repositories owned by six accounts this index did not hold. The accounts are recorded here as people the persona worked beside, not as further accounts of the persona: each commits under its own address and name, and nothing read so far shows one hand behind them.

Three of the six were created on one day. github.com/loveFeynman (account id 95080253) was created at 10:53 UTC on 26 November 2021, github.com/kdbvier (95093693) at 15:34, and github.com/nightskydev (95094109) at 15:42, eight minutes after kdbvier. github.com/sheriff-rango (95250818) followed on 29 November 2021.

The work is contemporaneous, not copied. In kdbvier/steampunks, kdbvier signed 21 commits and vigorousdeveloper 11 between 7 and 20 June 2022, and in kdbvier/Juno-Farming vigorousdeveloper signed 12 between 15 and 23 June 2022, followed by Jason07250000 in July. kdbvier/binance-trading-bot holds only the persona's commits, from January and April 2022. In nightskydev/picasso_frontend, created 19 June 2022, nightfury1111111111 signed 35 commits with linjay0208@gmail.com (the nightfury1111111111 account has since been deleted), the address every commit of nightskydev's own is signed with, while vigorousdeveloper signed 12 and kdbvier 6 over the same weeks; nightskydev/picasso_contract holds only the persona's commits. loveFeynman created mirror_protocol_stake_withdraw on 19 January 2022 and the persona committed into it as Eric Liu two days later; in loveFeynman/maui-frontend the two alternate across 2 to 5 January 2022. loveFeynman signs its own commits wando0226@gmail.com and willyu226@gmail.com under the names loveFeynman, wando and William Yu, and four commits signed William Yu with wando0226@gmail.com sit in vigorousdeveloper/NFT-AUCTION, dated 9 to 12 February 2022. sheriff-rango signed at least 99 commits in kdbvier/nfthope between 14 July and 13 September 2022. In frozenflux2/Solana_FE, created 23 February 2024, SuperVenus0725 committed with both of the persona's addresses in March 2024 beside frozenflux2's own aurora518star.com@gmail.com.

The follow graph agrees. SuperVenus0725 and loveFeynman follow each other, as do loveFeynman and sheriff-rango; vigorousdeveloper follows loveFeynman, kdbvier and nightskydev; kdbvier follows loveFeynman and SuperVenus0725.

Code also moved from these accounts into the persona's portfolio and back. loveFeynman's human_marketplace, first committed 13 August 2022, reappears with its history in SuperVenus0725/humanmarket (created 24 October 2022), sheriff-rango/HumansMarketplace and Calebtan978/HumansMarketplace. sheriff-rango created 24 repositories on 14 November 2022, 14 of which carry Jason07250000 commits from June 2022, and Calebtan978 holds eight carrying the same address.

Calebtan978 is filed on weaker ground than the other five. Its repositories are copies rather than shared work, created in May 2023 over commits from 2022. What adds to it is the account itself, id 132147781, created at 14:02 UTC on 29 April 2023, four minutes after github.com/niceDeve (132147539), which this index holds from Coinmonks' reporting on DPRK-linked GitHub activity.

An innocent reading was considered and set aside. A client who hires a contractor also creates repositories that the contractor then commits into, and nextnet-works, a company organisation with 266 repositories into which both SuperVenus0725 and loveFeynman committed in 2023, is left out for that reason. The six accounts above do not fit that reading: three were created within five hours of one another, they hold one another's code as portfolio, and they follow one another. KentaMori115 is also left out, because its only link is a 2023 copy of Juno-Farming carrying the persona's 2022 commits, which is how a copied repository looks.

Re-signing a copied history is not an accident of forking, which keeps the original authors, and copying a public project is not in itself suspect. unattributed.label: Trojanized palooza repository on the togetherlabsinchub account and its BeaverTail C2
unattributed.note: Endpoint telemetry from a developer who downloaded the main-branch archive of togetherlabsinchub/palooza from GitHub, reported to this site in October 2026, shows the project started with node server.js and then a Node.js child process run inline with node -e, carrying a campaign identifier, a numeric key and the C2 address http://151.80.76.64:1224/. That shape, an inline loader calling back to port 1224 and identifying itself to the server, is the BeaverTail first stage of the Contagious Interview campaign, delivered as a coding exercise in a fake job interview. The account name borrows that of Together Labs, Inc., a real company with no part in this; impersonating a real employer is the campaign's usual lure. By 26 October 2026 the account and the repository both returned not found through the GitHub API, and the Wayback Machine holds no capture of either, so the repository is listed as a removed link. Nothing from it was downloaded or run. Maltrail's Lazarus trail list carries 151.80.76.64 on ports 1224 and 3333 (the BeaverTail and InvisibleFerret ports), together with 151.80.76.66 and 151.80.76.67 on the same two ports. All three sit on OVH in Roubaix, rented through the Windows VPS reseller RDP Quick with remote desktop open. Shodan's InternetDB on 26 October 2026 showed a Node.js Express server on 151.80.76.64 port 3333 and on 151.80.76.66 port 1224, so at least two of the three were serving that day.

unattributed.label: Four interview-exercise repositories carrying the ip-check-encrypted loader, and their C2
unattributed.note:
Found on 27 October 2026 by searching GitHub code for the loader that bryanchriswhite's dev-trap-dossiers documents as the realfraction generation of the Contagious Interview campaign: a backend file that holds a base64-encoded URL ending /api/ip-check-encrypted/<id>, posts the whole of process.env to it with the header x-secret-header: secret, and runs the reply with new Function("require", ...). Each of the three repositories below carries that loader, read as text and never run.

Qevoratrix-live-coding is a GitHub organization created on 20 October 2026 that the same day published six repositories named for languages (react, go, rust, java, solidity, node), the shape of a live-coding interview exercise. In react, backend/src/services/errorHandler.service.config.js decodes to https://www.jitnad.lol/api/ip-check-encrypted/3aeb34a39; the file's only commit is dated 3 September 2026 and attributed to a real developer, whose history the repository copies. stockx-fi, an organization created on 3 August 2026, holds stockx_v1, whose backend/src/compliance/complianceService.js decodes to https://www.ipregionchecker.org/api/ip-check-encrypted/3aeb34a32. 0xbrentfi, a user account created on 21 February 2026 and displaying the name Brent Phelps, holds StockX_PoC_1.03 with the same file decoding to https://www.ipregionchecker.org/api/ip-check-encrypted/3aeb34a37; dev-trap-dossiers already lists that account among the realfraction repositories, and Maltrail's Lazarus trail list carries ipregionchecker.org. The StockX proof-of-concept is the lure that write-up describes, and its first C2 was ipregionchecker.com. jitnad.lol was registered through Dynadot on 23 October 2026, the day the loader was pushed to the repository, and appears in no published source found on 27 October 2026.

The same search found jamesm-dev/NitroGem, a neutralized copy of the NitroGem trading-bot lure published for study, whose report gives the original's stage-one C2 as https://locate-my-ip.vercel.app/api/ip-check-encrypted/3aeb34a31; dev-trap-dossiers lists the original, TechByteX/NitroGem, in the cluster. The study copy itself is not filed.

Not carried: the commit authors of all three repositories are real developers (one at Uniswap) whose commit history was copied into the lure, the usual way these repositories borrow credibility.
